questionText: When is a country's 'Balance of Trade' considered to be 'Favourable'?

options.text: Favourable when imports exceed exports tenfold
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Favourable when the value of exports exceeds imports; Unfavourable when the value of imports exceeds exports
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Balance of Trade.

options.text: Favourable only when a country stops all foreign trade
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Unfavourable when exports exceed imports by 100%
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Transport, Communication and International Trade (Balance of Trade):
Favourable when the value of exports exceeds imports; Unfavourable when the value of imports exceeds exports

Detailed Analysis:
Balance of trade is the difference between the monetary value of exports and imports. If the value of exports is greater than imports, it is a Favourable (positive) balance. If imports exceed exports, it is an Unfavourable (negative) balance.
Hence, Option A is correct.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
